answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond that is forfeited if it repeatedly fails randomly assigned, costly-to-fake tasks, such as delivering a signed response to a fresh challenge before a deadline. Honest agents recover their stake; creating many fake agents multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of slashing, so identities are no longer cheap. An orchard marketplace might route tasks through a vertex, while a pearl-sized bond would deter little unless calibrated to the value an attacker can extract.
